strategy.headline: Contrarian but not stupid: when an underdog is worth taking
strategy.summary: In a pick'em the favourite is usually the crowd's pick, so a correct underdog is what separates a leaderboard entry from the pack. The trade-off only pays when the underdog is backed by a verifiable reason and the price still leaves room. The rules below are project strategy, not verified outcomes.

rules.rule: Take the underdog when a roster change is recent and structural, not cosmetic.
rules.why: A new in-game leader, a new star and a new coach inside one split means an unproven system, new communication and a short practice window. Aurora's 2026 rebuild is the day-one example.
rules.verify: Official organisation announcements, the transfer timeline and the team's own statements, then confirm the current five on a fixture-specific source.

rules.rule: Take the underdog when the favourite is demonstrably fatigued and the market has not repriced.
rules.why: Deep runs plus travel compress preparation. A favourite whose price already fell has no contrarian value left.
rules.verify: Compare the favourite's recent tournament load and travel from results pages, then check whether the offered price still reflects the earlier reputation.

rules.rule: Prefer underdogs whose chance is roughly one in five or better, and expect to lose most of them.
rules.why: A 20-40% pick that wins is worth the same single point as a favourite but moves you past everyone who copied the crowd. Below that band the pick is a lottery ticket, not an edge.
rules.verify: Use the sourced market probability on the picks page. Where no market exists, use the labelled research tier and treat it as low confidence.

rules.rule: Never size up a contrarian pick on an identity or a number you cannot source.
rules.why: Renamed teams, academy squads and unclear aliases are exactly where a whole pick'em slips away on a wrong team.
rules.verify: The identity register in this project requires an exact opponent and UTC start before any alias is used.

rules.rule: Limit how many contrarian swings you take per slate.
rules.why: Stacking four underdogs multiplies variance instead of climbing the leaderboard.
rules.verify: Count the contrarian picks shown in the screen below; treat anything beyond one or two as exposure, not insight.

unverified: This project does not collect Hotspawn's pick'em scoring rules, so no claim is made about how many points a correct underdog is worth relative to a favourite.
No calibrated historical model exists here: contrarian picks are market-implied plus sourced context, and are not a promise of profit or of a higher leaderboard position.

contrarian.why: The framework only pays when an underdog has a verifiable reason and the price still leaves room. 9z beat this exact opponent 2-0 on 14 October, took a map off the tournament’s strongest group winner, and current sources put 9z between 31.0% and 34.15%—inside the 20–40% band. Aurora are the better-ranked team and answered their critics on day two, which is the risk side of the trade.
not_stupid_check: Price still in the 20-40% band rather than a lottery ticket (rule 3).
The reason is a repeatable head-to-head result and a map win, not a rumour (rules 1 and 4).
Only one contrarian swing is in band on this slate, so exposure stays at one (rule 5).
contrarian.limits: This is analysis of dated source-specific market lines, not a prediction. The automated Hotspawn row uses its own validated exchange quote and refresh/expiry rules; the other book is not blended into it. If the 9z price falls below roughly 20%, the framework says the contrarian price no longer pays and the live board should take precedence.
